cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Feudalism ≠ democracy – a social system based on landholding and vassal duty.

p.em: Example: Technofeudalism describes digital platforms acting as digital landlords.

cosy-blockquote.p: Attention economy ≠ free exchange – the perspective treating human attention as a scarce commodity.

p.em: Example: Social media platforms trade in the attention economy.

cosy-blockquote.p: Platform ≠ independent site – a digital service providing a foundation for application hosting.

p.em: Example: Tech platforms rent digital space to creators.

cosy-blockquote.p: Monopolize ≠ share – to obtain exclusive possession or control of a market.

p.em: Example: Big tech firms monopolize user attention data.

cosy-blockquote.p: Exploitation ≠ fairness – the action of treating someone unfairly to benefit from their work.

p.em: Example: Constant notifications lead to emotional exploitation.

cosy-blockquote.p: Engagement ≠ disconnection – the state of being actively involved with digital media.

p.em: Example: Algorithms prioritize high outrage for maximum engagement.

cosy-blockquote.p: Surveillance ≠ privacy – close observation, especially of a suspected spy or user.

p.em: Example: Surveillance capitalism tracks online behavior.

cosy-blockquote.p: Addiction ≠ moderation – the state of being enslaved to a habit or practice.

p.em: Example: Infinite scrolling features trigger device addiction.

cosy-blockquote.p: Vassal ≠ sovereign – a person or entity in a subordinate position.

p.em: Example: Users act like digital vassals generating data for platform owners.

cosy-blockquote.p: Reclaim ≠ surrender – to retrieve or recover something lost.

p.em: Example: We must reclaim control over our daily attention span.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
How does modern corporate feudalism describe the power of tech giants over online users?
★ Do you feel big tech platforms control digital public spaces?

Why has human attention become the most valuable commodity in the attention economy?
★ How many hours a day do you spend on screen-based media?

How does a dominant digital platform lock users into its ecosystem?
★ Which social platform or app ecosystem do you use most?

Why do large tech monopolies attempt to monopolize user data and online interactions?
★ Are you concerned about data privacy monopolization?

How does algorithmic commercial exploitation turn user content into corporate profit?
★ Do you feel social media networks treat users as digital laborers?

What design tricks maximize digital engagement and keep users scrolling endlessly?
★ Have you disabled push notifications to reduce screen time?

How does pervasive digital surveillance affect human online behavior and self-expression?
★ Do you feel watched when targeted ads match your private conversations?

What behavioral signs indicate growing smartphone addiction in daily life?
★ How long can you go without checking your smartphone?

Why are users compared to modern digital vassals working for tech platforms?
★ Do you feel reliant on proprietary tech services?

How can individuals reclaim their attention span and mental autonomy from screens?
★ What boundaries have you set for your screen time?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Look at the prompt and discuss your response with your teacher:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
Modern technofeudalism threatens democratic freedom more than traditional economic monopolies. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Concerned about tech oligarchs influencing public debate?

Participating in the digital attention economy makes genuine focus impossible for most people. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Struggle with digital distraction during work?

Every major tech platform should be regulated as a public utility service. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Should platforms like search and social media be public utilities?

Preventing tech giants from trying to monopolize user data requires strict anti-trust laws. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Support breaking up big tech monopolies?

Monetizing user data without direct payment is ethical exploitation that must be banned. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Should users be paid for their personal data?

Designing apps for addictive engagement should be illegal for software companies. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Support bans on infinite scroll and auto-play features?

Mass digital surveillance destroys personal privacy and undermines free speech. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Value online privacy over convenience?

Recognizing smartphone addiction as a medical issue is necessary for public health. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Should tech addiction treatment be offered by healthcare?

Refusing to act as a digital vassal to tech platforms requires adopting open-source tools. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Use open-source software or private platforms?

Empowering people to reclaim their focus is the biggest educational challenge of our century. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Should focus training be taught in schools?
